name: Hard Currency
tagline: A product-defined currency bought with real money and held as a stored balance until it's spent on something the product defines.
desc: Hard currency sits between a payment and whatever the payment is actually for. The user buys units, the units sit in a stored balance, and the exchange for an item, service, or access right happens later, sometimes across several separate purchases. That gap is what makes it different from a straight purchase: money converts into a product-defined unit first, and the unit is what gets spent. The same balance can also be earned, gifted, or bundled into a subscription without losing its hard-currency status, as long as a real-money path into it exists somewhere.
principle: Buying the currency and spending the currency are two separate decisions. Once the purchase is made, every later exchange draws on a balance rather than a price, which is what keeps hard currency spending feeling lighter than the equivalent direct purchases would.
warn: The distinguishing question is whether the balance behaves like money held for the user, refundable and spendable outside the product, or like a product-defined unit meant only for internal exchange. The prepaid-wallet case is the one to check against before applying this label.
variants: Direct-purchase, sold in defined packages for money
Subscription-granted, an active plan periodically adds to the balance
Earnable, the same currency can also be obtained without paying
Restricted, spendable only within a defined feature or area
lifecycle: Effective across all lifecycle stages once a purchase path exists. Most consequential right after a first purchase, when spending shifts from real money to a stored balance.
